summary: createAiChatHandler reads a view context (what the user had open when sending the newest message) from the body field glirastesViewContext and gives it to the model as a data block. On by default; nothing sends the field yet, so an unchanged app sees no change.
howTo: Nothing to do. The browser side follows in a later release. To prepare: viewContext: false turns it off (null counts as not set); viewContext: { types, maxEntries, facts: { order: z.object({ status: z.string() }) } } narrows the accepted entity types (by default every type the request's tools declare with outputEntities / inputEntities), the entries per message and the facts kept (only for a type with a schema here). history must be 'none' for now; an invalid option throws when the handler is created. The runtime container turns it off until its option chat.viewContext comes. With piiShield the labels of the kept entries are cleaned and shielded uncut, then cut to 60 characters (the cut leaves no fragment of a value), and the other values are shielded like tool results: at most two anonymizeResult calls per request (audit: anonymize-result, counted in totalToolCalls), then checked again; a label over 512 code points after cleaning (or 4,096 before) is dropped. Known limit of the PII shield (anonymizeResult, since 0.1.0, as for tool results; fixed in #197): a short value the session knows inside a longer one can leave part of the longer in plain text (label Kunde max@firma.de with id johannes.max@firma.de gives johannes.<pseudonym>). The block has at most 2,966 characters (roughly 850 tokens when full); maxEntries and facts make it smaller. Only the built-in stream handler adds the block; continuations, guardrail-blocked requests, clarification answers, direct commands and a custom streamHandler get none; guardrails and hideIds do not see it.
